cards.explanation: The answer is summit. Isaiah says the crown is "…set on the summit above the fertile valley…" That's the top of the hill, with the whole valley spread out below. I think it's the kind of spot where you can see everybody and everybody can see you.

The answer is a fading flower. Isaiah calls it "…the fading flower of his glorious splendor…" A crown sounds like it will last forever, but a fading flower is already on its way out. He says it again in verse 4, friends, so I think he wants you to catch it.

The answer is a hailstorm or destructive tempest. Isaiah says the Lord's strong one will be "Like a hailstorm or destructive tempest…" Then he keeps piling it on: "…like a driving rain or flooding downpour…" He doesn't stop at one storm, friends. He keeps going until you can hear the sky coming apart.

The answer is False. Isaiah says the Lord's strong one "…will smash that crown to the ground." So the crown doesn't get lifted up. It gets knocked down from the summit, and the storm pictures show how hard it hits.

The answer is a ripe fig before the summer harvest. Isaiah says the fading flower "…will be like a ripe fig before the summer harvest…" A fig that ripens early is ready to be picked right now. I think that shows how easily this crown gets taken.
The answer is False. Isaiah says "Whoever sees it will take it in his hand and swallow it." The fig doesn't get left hanging. Whoever spots it takes it right away.

The answer is the remnant of His people. Isaiah says "On that day the LORD of Hosts will be a crown of glory, a diadem of splendor to the remnant of His people…" Ephraim's drunkards have a crown that fades. The LORD Himself is the crown for the remnant, friends. That's a big switch.

The answer is justice. Isaiah says the LORD will be "…a spirit of justice to him who sits in judgment…" Whoever sits in judgment needs justice, and here the LORD Himself is that spirit. It's a good thing to have when people are looking to you for a ruling.

The answer is True. Isaiah says the LORD will be "…a strength to those who repel the onslaught at the gate." The gate is where people stand when trouble comes at them. On that day, they won't be standing there on their own strength.

The answer is priests. Isaiah says "Priests and prophets reel from strong drink and are befuddled by wine." Priests and prophets are named right there in the verse. That's a heavy part of the passage, friends, so I think it's worth slowing down on.

The answer is True. Isaiah says the priests and prophets are "…muddled in their visions and stumbling in their judgments." The strong drink has them muddled and stumbling. Verse 7 says this about priests and prophets together.

The answer is infants just weaned from milk. The text asks, "To infants just weaned from milk? To babies removed from the breast?" Those are the people it names, and they're the littlest ones around. It's asked as a question, so I'll leave the answer where the text leaves it.

The answer is with mocking lips and foreign tongues. Isaiah says "…with mocking lips and foreign tongues, He will speak to this people" That's the way verse 11 gives, friends. Verse 12 says these are the people to whom He has said, "This is the place of rest…"
The answer is False. After the offer of rest, the verse says "But they would not listen." The offer was on the table, and they would not listen. I think that's a quiet, sad little sentence.

The answer is stumbling backward. Isaiah says the word of the LORD will become that line "so that they will go stumbling backward…" The people don't move forward, friends. They go backward, and they stumble while they do it.
The answer is captured. Isaiah says they "…will be injured, ensnared, and captured." Three words, and each one is worse than the one before. It's a heavy way for the passage to close.
